column1: 22:1|For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.|Keeps the interval of peace.
22:2|In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to visit the king of Israel.|Identifies both kingdoms without inserting a motive.
22:3|Israel’s king said to his servants, “You know Ramoth-gilead belongs to us. Why are we doing nothing to take it back from the king of Aram?”|Makes the reproach audible within the royal claim.

22:4|He asked Jehoshaphat, “Will you join me in battle at Ramoth-gilead?” Jehoshaphat answered Israel’s king, “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.”|Retains the threefold pledge of solidarity.
22:5|But Jehoshaphat said to Israel’s king, “First, please seek the LORD’s word.”|Clarifies the requested order of action.

22:6|Israel’s king gathered about four hundred prophets and asked, “Should I go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or hold back?” “Go,” they said. “The Lord will give it into the king’s hand.”|Keeps approximate count and Adonai designation.
22:7|Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no other prophet of the LORD here whom we can consult?”|Preserves another prophet rather than denying all prophetic status.

22:8|Israel’s king answered, “There is one more man through whom we can consult the LORD, Micaiah son of Imlah. But I hate him. He never prophesies good for me, only disaster.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not speak that way.”|Distinguishes Ahab’s complaint from the narrator’s judgment.
22:9|Then Israel’s king called a court official. “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly,” he said.|Court role translated without settling bodily status.

22:10|Israel’s king and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat on their thrones, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor by Samaria’s gate. All the prophets were prophesying before them.|Makes the public setting clear.

22:11|Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself iron horns. He declared, “This is what the LORD says: With these you will gore Aram until you finish them off.”|Preserves enacted animal imagery and destruction.
22:12|All the prophets said the same: “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed! The LORD will give it into the king’s hand.”|Retains their united prediction and divine name.

22:13|The messenger who went to summon Micaiah told him, “The prophets are speaking with one voice in the king’s favor. Please let your word agree with theirs. Speak favorably.”|Exposes pressure to conform without adding motive.
22:14|Micaiah answered, “As the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me.”|Keeps oath and stated prophetic obligation.

22:15|When he reached the king, the king asked, “Micaiah, should we go to war at Ramoth-gilead, or hold back?” He answered, “Go and succeed! The LORD will give it into the king’s hand.”|Leaves apparent irony to the following exchange.
22:16|The king replied, “How many times must I put you under oath to tell me only the truth in the LORD’s name?”|Keeps the king’s challenge and oath language.

22:17|Then Micaiah said, “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The LORD said, ‘These have no master. Let each return home in peace.’”|Preserves the shepherd image and peace announcement.
22:18|Israel’s king said to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell you? He prophesies nothing good for me, only disaster.”|Repeats Ahab’s accusation as his interpretation.

22:19|Micaiah continued, “Then hear the LORD’s word. I saw the LORD seated on his throne, with all heaven’s army standing beside him, to his right and left.|Keeps the heavenly council distinct from earthly thrones.
22:20|The LORD asked, ‘Who will entice Ahab to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ One proposed this, another that.|Retains divine initiative in the disturbing vision.
22:21|Then the spirit came forward and stood before the LORD. ‘I will entice him,’ it said. ‘How?’ the LORD asked.|Uses the full original Hebrew record, including the question.

22:22|It answered, ‘I will go and become a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ The LORD said, ‘You will entice him and succeed. Go and do it.’|Preserves authorization of deception without theological repair.
22:23|So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours. The LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”|Keeps the vision’s application attributed to Micaiah.
22:24|Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek. “Which way did the LORD’s spirit pass from me to speak to you?” he asked.|Retains the blow and derisive question.
22:25|Micaiah answered, “You will see on the day you go into an inner room to hide.”|Keeps future answer without adding its occasion.
22:26|Israel’s king said, “Take Micaiah back to Amon the city governor and Joash the king’s son.|Preserves both custodians and Joash’s title.
22:27|Tell them, ‘The king says: Put this man in prison. Give him meager bread and water until I return in peace.’”|Makes the deprivation concrete and repeats peace.
22:28|Micaiah said, “If you really return in peace, the LORD has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Listen, all you peoples!”|Retains the public challenge and broad final address.
22:29|Israel’s king and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.|Keeps the narrative resumption spare.

22:30|Israel’s king told Jehoshaphat, “I will enter the battle in disguise, but you wear your robes.” So Israel’s king disguised himself and went into battle.|Clarifies who disguises himself without supplying a scheme.
22:31|The king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, “Fight no one, small or great, except the king of Israel.”|Retains exact command and number.
22:32|When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “That must be Israel’s king!” They turned to attack him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.|Does not invent the words of his cry.
22:33|When they saw he was not Israel’s king, they stopped pursuing him.|Keeps recognition as the stated reason.

22:34|But a man drew his bow without a particular target and struck Israel’s king between the armor’s fittings and breastplate. The king told his chariot driver, “Turn around and take me out of the fighting. I am wounded.”|Preserves untargeted shot and uncertain armor detail.

22:35|The battle grew fierce that day. The king was held upright in his chariot facing Aram. He died that evening, and blood from his wound ran into the chariot’s floor.|Retains bodily injury and continued exposure.
22:36|At sunset a shout went through the camp: “Everyone to his town! Everyone to his own land!”|Keeps the twofold dismissal.
22:37|The king was dead. They brought him to Samaria and buried him there.|Clarifies transport of the dead king.
22:38|They washed the chariot at Samaria’s pool, where prostitutes bathed, and dogs licked his blood, just as the LORD had said.|Retains prostitutes and location without harmonizing Naboth’s oracle.

22:39|The rest of Ahab’s deeds, everything he did, the ivory house he built, and all the towns he built—are they not written in the annals of the kings of Israel?|Preserves the source notice and ivory house.
22:40|Ahab lay down with his ancestors, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.|Keeps the ancestral death formula.
22:41|Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.|Retains the regnal synchronism.
22:42|Jehoshaphat was thirty-five when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.|Preserves age, reign, and maternal lineage.

22:43|He followed the whole course of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the LORD’s eyes. Yet the high places remained; the people still sacrificed and burned offerings there.|Binds both Hebrew records 43–44 to the inherited public label.
22:44|Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.|Retains peace between the kingdoms.
22:45|The rest of Jehoshaphat’s deeds, his achievements, and the wars he fought—are they not written in the annals of the kings of Judah?|Keeps the source referral and military record.
22:46|He removed from the land the remaining male shrine attendants who had survived from his father Asa’s days.|Matches the qualified cult-term choice in earlier chapters.
22:47|There was no king in Edom; a deputy ruled as king.|Preserves the distinction without identifying an overlord.
22:48|Jehoshaphat built Tarshish ships to sail to Ophir for gold. But they never sailed, because they were wrecked at Ezion-geber.|Follows the read forms and keeps the failed voyage.
22:49|Then Ahaziah son of Ahab told Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants sail with yours.” But Jehoshaphat refused.|Does not import a different sequence from Chronicles.

22:50|Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David his ancestor. His son Jehoram became king in his place.|Clarifies ancestral David rather than immediate father.
22:51|Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. He ruled Israel for two years.|Preserves both chronological statements.
22:52|He did evil in the LORD’s eyes, following his father, his mother, and Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin.|Retains the three influences and corporate consequence.
22:53|He served Baal and bowed down to him, provoking the LORD, Israel’s God, just as his father had done.|Closes with worship, anger, and continuity.
